title: Stock: a box side a few ulps longer than a whole number of cells gets an extra column of material

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
### What happened

The column count of a stock box is a plain ceiling: `(extent / cell).ceil()`. A box side that is a few ulps longer than a whole number of cells gets one more column, although the box edge falls only femtometres into it.

Example: a 12.7 mm side read two ulps long (`f64::from_bits(12.7f64.to_bits() + 2)`) over a 0.254 mm cell gives a ratio of 50 plus about 1e-14. The ceiling gives 51 columns, not 50. The box edge falls about 3.6e-15 mm into column 51.

A side reads a few ulps long after a rigid move in floating point, for example a blank moved into a setup frame and back.

Three places count the columns this way:
- `Dexel::block` (column stock).
- The cell-ceiling gate of the field block (`backend_build.rs`).
- The exact carry read `History::read` (`carry_exact.rs`).

Effects:
- Column 51 is a full cell. Material stands up to one cell (0.254 mm) past the box edge.
- The carry read of the same box also counts 51 columns.
- A mesh export that clips the last column to the box edge gets a column about 3.6e-15 mm wide. A weld at 1e-8 mm collapses its facets: edges on three or more facets and zero-area facets. A mesh check then rejects the stock. We saw this on our fork's own mesh export.

Expected: a box side within a relative 1e-9 of a whole number of cells gets that whole number of columns. A real part of a cell still gets its column.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `let x0 = -f64::from_bits(12.7f64.to_bits() + 2);`
2. `let stock = Stock::block(Backend::Column, x0, 0.0, -0.0, 1.0, 5.0, 0.254).unwrap();`
3. Read the column arm: `nx` is 51. Expected: 50.
4. `stock.top(0.1, 0.5)` is 5.0. Expected: NaN, because x = 0.1 mm is outside the box.

### Proposed fix

One shared count, `cells_across(extent, cell)`, in `stock_sim::kernel`:

```rust
let r = extent / cell;
let k = r.round();
if k >= 1.0 && (r - k).abs() <= 1e-9 * k { k } else { r.ceil() }
```

Use it in `Dexel::block`, in the field block's cell-ceiling gate, and in `History::read` (with `.max(1)`, so a thin box keeps one column). We have this change on our fork with four pinning tests in `stock_sim/cell_count_tests.rs`. Each test fails on the plain ceiling (51 against 50). We claim this issue and will open a draft PR from a branch `issue/N-whole-cell-count`.

### Version and OS

v0.26.0 (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `P3` (wrong stock at a box edge, with a workaround: snap the box to whole cells before the block), `effort:high` (stock simulation is under the safety floor), `area:sim`.

Done means: a pinning test makes a column block from a box side two ulps longer than 50 cells and gets 50 columns, no material past the box edge, and the same count from the carry read.
